qualification: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger qualify through constitutionally designated working-language use of French, even though their current constitutions distinguish it from official national languages. Luxembourg also qualifies through statutory legislative and administrative use. Mauritius qualifies through constitutionally authorized French in the National Assembly (Section 49).

sources.name: Niger Official Journal · 2025 Refoundation Charter, Article 12
Luxembourg Government · statutory court and administrative languages

qualification: Constitutional official-language wording is not required. Argentina, Chile, Mexico and Uruguay qualify through national statutory or legally prescribed public use of Spanish. Paraguay and Equatorial Guinea also explicitly recognize Spanish as official.

sources.name: Argentina · National Civil and Commercial Procedure Code, Article 115
Chile Directorate of Labour · ORD. 881 (2024), Spanish in official documents
Mexico · Linguistic Rights Act, Articles 4 and 7
Paraguay Chamber of Deputies · Constitution, Article 140

qualification: Luxembourg qualifies through legally authorized national administrative and judicial use of German. Belgium has three official languages with territorially regulated use; regional-only German in Italy does not qualify.

sources.name: Luxembourg Government · statutory court and administrative languages

qualification: Sweden calls Swedish its principal language. Section 10 of the Language Act also prescribes Swedish for courts, administrative authorities and other public bodies, so Sweden qualifies through government use. Swedish is also a national official language in Finland.

sources.name: Swedish Parliament · Language Act 2009:600, Sections 4 and 10

qualification: Czech qualifies through Section 16 of Act 500/2004, which prescribes Czech for administrative proceedings and documents. An explicit constitutional official-language clause is not required.

sources.name: Czech Financial Analytical Office · Administrative Procedure Code, Section 16
